Task: Sync skills/service-area pickers with the real catalog
Description: provider-web's SkillsSection and ServiceAreasSection (frontend/provider-web/src/app/(provider)/profile/_components/) require providers to hand-type raw categoryId/serviceId and city/zone/pincode GUIDs - confirmed via the component's own doc comment ('id typed by hand, no catalog lookup endpoint in this contract'). provider-api has no categories/services or geography listing endpoint at all (only consumer-api/admin-api do). Add a read-only provider-api catalog/geography lookup (or expose consumer-api's existing public endpoints for provider-web to call directly) and replace the free-text inputs with real dropdowns showing actual category/service/city names, so provider-declared skills and coverage areas are guaranteed to reference entities that exist in the same catalog/geography tables customers and admins see.

Design and implement a single login entry point shared by customer-web, admin-web, and provider-web, redirecting to the correct app/dashboard based on account type after authentication (rather than three separate /login pages on three separate origins/ports with no relationship). Needs a decision on approach before implementation: (a) one login app on its own subdomain issuing role-scoped tokens and redirecting to the right origin, or (b) a shared login route proxied identically into all three Next.js apps that calls the right backend (consumer-api/admin-api/provider-api) based on a mode selector. Affects JWT audience handling (Nestly.Customers/Nestly.AdminUsers/Nestly.Providers are currently three independent schemes per DependencyInjection.cs) and CORS config per app - needs an architecture decision, not just a UI change.
